# @zakkster/lite-o1

Version: 0.4.0
License: MIT (c) Zahary Shinikchiev <shinikchiev@yahoo.com>
Runtime dependencies: none. ESM only. ASCII-only source. sideEffects: false.
Node: >= 18.

## What it is

A tree-shakeable, zero-GC family of O(1) data structures that PROVES its
constant instead of asserting it. The complexity class is the product: every hot
op is O(1) worst-case (or O(1)-amortized where stated) and allocates zero bytes
after construction, and a shipped witness harness demonstrates the flat
throughput curve against a built-in foil.

v0.4.0 ships four members: SparseSet, RingDeque, UnionFind, and MonoDeque. They
share no mutable module state, so a bundler that imports one drops the others
(tree-shakeable).

## Exports (from the single main file O1.js)

- `SparseSet` -- class. A zero-GC O(1) integer set over [0, universe).
- `RingDeque` -- class. A zero-GC O(1) fixed-capacity numeric double-ended queue.
- `UnionFind` -- class. A zero-GC near-O(1) amortized disjoint-set forest.
- `MonoDeque` -- class. A zero-GC O(1)-amortized monotonic deque for
  sliding-window min / max.
- `VERSION` -- string, '0.4.0'.

## SparseSet

    new SparseSet(universe, capacity = universe)

- universe: exclusive key ceiling; integer in [1, 2^32]. Sizes the sparse array.
- capacity: max live members; integer in [1, universe], default universe. Sizes
  the dense array.
- Constructor throws a [lite-o1] RangeError on a non-integer / out-of-range arg.

Hot surface (all O(1) worst-case, zero allocation):

- add(k) -> this        Insert; idempotent. Throws [lite-o1] on a bad key
                        (not an integer in [0, universe): -1, 1.5, NaN, null,
                        k === universe) or when a NEW key exceeds capacity.
                        Re-adding a present key when full is a no-op.
- has(k) -> boolean     Membership. A bad key is ABSENT, never a throw. null is
                        not zero: has(null) is false even when 0 is a member.
- delete(k) -> boolean  Remove by swapping the last dense entry into the hole and
                        fixing its back-pointer. true iff k was present. Never throws.
- clear() -> void       Empty in O(1): resets the live count, zeroes NO store.
                        Stale sparse pointers fail the has() cross-check.
- forEach(fn) -> void   Iterate present keys in insertion order, alloc-free.
                        fn is (key, set).
- [Symbol.iterator]()   Iterate present keys in insertion order.
- size (getter)         Live member count.
- capacity (getter)     Max live members as constructed.

Membership invariant (the whole trick):

    has(k) == sparse[k] < n && dense[sparse[k]] === k

The cross-check rejects stale sparse pointers, which is why clear() can be O(1)
and never zero a store.

## RingDeque

    new RingDeque(capacity)

- capacity: requested max elements; integer in [1, 2^31]. ROUNDS UP to the next
  power of two (>= requested); the capacity getter reports the rounded value.
- Constructor throws a [lite-o1] RangeError on a non-integer / out-of-range /
  non-number arg (typeof-guarded before any coercion; message via String(x)).
- Substrate: ONE Float64Array (numeric values only), head + count representation.
  The physical slot for logical offset i from the front is store[(head + i) & MASK],
  MASK = capacity - 1; wrap is a single & (power-of-two modulo), no branch.

Hot surface (all O(1) worst-case, zero allocation):

- pushFront(v) -> this   Push v onto the front. Throws [lite-o1] when FULL (a
                         byte-identical no-op) or on a non-clean value.
- pushBack(v) -> this    Push v onto the back. Same fail-closed policy.
- popFront() -> number|undefined  Remove+return the front; undefined on empty (never throws).
- popBack()  -> number|undefined  Remove+return the back; undefined on empty (never throws).
- peekFront() -> number|undefined Front without removing; undefined on empty.
- peekBack()  -> number|undefined Back without removing; undefined on empty.
- clear() -> void        Empty in O(1): resets head + count, touches NO store
                         (numbers retain no references, so nothing to zero).
- forEach(fn) -> void    Iterate live elements front->back, alloc-free.
                         fn is (value, index, deque).
- [Symbol.iterator]()    Iterate live elements front->back.
- size (getter)          Live element count.
- capacity (getter)      Max elements (power-of-two, rounded up from requested).

Value contract (LOCKED): a pushed value must be typeof 'number' AND not NaN.
Rejected (throws [lite-o1]): null, undefined, string, Symbol, BigInt, object, NaN.
Accepted: any finite number, and +Infinity / -Infinity (typeof number, not NaN).
The typeof guard runs FIRST so a Symbol / BigInt never reaches arithmetic.

## UnionFind

    new UnionFind(n)

- n: fixed element count; integer in [1, 2^32-1]. Elements are [0, n).
- Constructor throws a [lite-o1] RangeError on a non-integer / out-of-range arg
  (Number.isInteger never coerces; message via String(n), Symbol/BigInt-safe).
- Substrate: TWO flat Uint32Array columns -- parent[i] (i's parent; i itself iff
  root) and size[root] (elements in that tree). Path halving on find + union by
  size bound any single op at O(alpha(n)) amortized (inverse Ackermann, <= ~4).

Hot surface (all O(1)-AMORTIZED, zero allocation):

- find(x) -> number      Root of x's component. Path halving flattens the walk in
                         place (no recursion, no stack array). Throws [lite-o1] on
                         a bad element (typeof-guarded before the coercing >>>).
- union(a,b) -> boolean  Merge a and b. true iff a real merge happened (they were
                         separate); false if already joined. Union by size. Guards
                         both endpoints. count-- exactly once per true merge.
- connected(a,b) -> boolean  find(a) === find(b). Both guarded via find.
- componentSize(x) -> number size[find(x)]. Guarded via find.
- count (getter)         Live component count. O(1), maintained (never scanned).
- capacity (getter)      Fixed element universe n. (No `size` getter -- it would
                         collide with the live-count meaning size has elsewhere.)
- reset() -> void        O(n) HONEST EXCEPTION: re-singleton every element
                         (parent[i]=i, size[i]=1, count=n). A single bulk pass over
                         the existing arrays -- allocates NOTHING, but is O(n), NOT
                         a zero-alloc-per-op hot path. Named reset(), not clear().
- forEachRoots(fn) -> void  O(n) FULL SCAN, alloc-free: fn(root, uf) per current
                         root. Documented exception, EXCLUDED from the
                         zero-alloc-per-op claims. fn is hoisted for zero alloc.
- roots() -> generator   O(n) scan; ALLOCATES a generator + {value,done} per step
                         by protocol (like [Symbol.iterator]) -- OUT of zero-alloc
                         claims. Use forEachRoots for the alloc-free scan.

Amortized honesty: a single find is NOT worst-case O(1) -- an adversarial
pre-halving chain is O(depth). The guarantee is AMORTIZED alpha(n); the witness
reports amortized throughput staying flat while a no-compression / no-union-by-size
foil (a degenerate chain) collapses.

## MonoDeque

    new MonoDeque(capacity, kind)

- capacity: max simultaneously-live entries; integer in [1, 2^31]. ROUNDS UP to
  the next power of two; the capacity getter reports the rounded value.
- kind: 'min' or 'max', FROZEN at construction (one monotone invariant per
  instance). Validated fail-closed (anything else throws [lite-o1]).
- Constructor throws a [lite-o1] RangeError on a bad capacity (non-integer /
  out-of-range / non-number, typeof-guarded before coercion) or a bad kind.
- Substrate: TWO parallel Float64Arrays (value + monotonic seq) inside a
  head + count power-of-two ring; wrap is a single & (capacity - 1). For 'min' the
  stored values are STRICTLY INCREASING front -> back (front is the window
  minimum); for 'max' strictly decreasing (front is the maximum). Seqs are always
  strictly increasing front -> back (FIFO insertion order).

Hot surface (push / evictOlderThan are O(1)-AMORTIZED; the reads are O(1)
worst-case; all zero allocation):

- push(v) -> seq          Assign the next monotonic seq, pop all DOMINATED back
                          entries (min: back.value >= v; max: back.value <= v),
                          then append. Returns the assigned seq. Each element is
                          pushed and popped at most once (amortized O(1); a single
                          push is O(k) worst-case). Fail closed: a non-clean value
                          throws [lite-o1] (typeof guard FIRST); a FULL ring throws
                          a byte-identical no-op; a seq past MAX_SEQ (2^53) throws.
- evictOlderThan(seq) -> void  Drop front entries whose stored seq <= seq (the
                          caller's window slide). O(1)-amortized. Validates the seq
                          arg fail-closed (typeof-number guard, NaN rejected).
- value() -> number|undefined   The current window extreme (front value). O(1).
                          undefined on empty, NEVER throws.
- frontSeq() -> number|undefined The seq of the current extreme. O(1). undefined
                          on empty.
- kind (getter)          The frozen 'min' | 'max' invariant.
- size (getter)          Live entry count.
- capacity (getter)      Max simultaneously-live entries (power-of-two, rounded up).
- clear() -> void        O(1): reset head + count + the seq counter, touch NO store
                          (numbers retain no references). The seq counter restarts at 0.
- forEach(fn) -> void    O(k) alloc-free scan front -> back; fn is (value, seq,
                          deque). A documented exception, EXCLUDED from the
                          zero-alloc-per-op claims.
- [Symbol.iterator]()    O(k) scan; the ONE per-protocol ALLOCATOR (yields a
                          [value, seq] tuple + a {value, done} per step) -- OUT of
                          the zero-alloc claims. Use forEach for the alloc-free scan.

Value contract (LOCKED, IDENTICAL to RingDeque): a pushed value must be
typeof 'number' AND not NaN. Rejected (throws [lite-o1]): null, undefined, string,
Symbol, BigInt, object (incl. one with a numeric valueOf), NaN. Accepted: any
finite number, and +Infinity / -Infinity. The typeof guard runs FIRST so a Symbol
/ BigInt never reaches arithmetic.

Windowing model: MonoDeque is a caller-driven PRIMITIVE, not a policy. push
appends and evictOlderThan drops what the caller has slid past, so one MonoDeque
serves any window rule (count-based, time-based, event-based): the deque owns the
monotone invariant, the caller owns which seqs are still in the window.

Amortized honesty: push is O(1) AMORTIZED, not worst-case -- a single push can pop
O(k) dominated back entries. The witness shows the amortized ops/ms staying flat
while a naive O(W)-window-rescan foil collapses, and reports the MAX single-op time
so a hidden worst-case spike shows as a tall bar. MAX_SEQ = 2^53 is the seq
ceiling (seqs live in a Float64 slot; past 2^53 push throws rather than lose
integer precision -- call clear() to reuse).

## Design bounds

- SparseSet valid key: integer in [0, universe).
- SparseSet fixed capacity: no silent growth; a new key past capacity throws.
- SparseSet fail closed on add, absent on query. null is never coerced to key 0.
- RingDeque fixed capacity (power-of-two, rounded up): push past full throws
  (fail closed); pop/peek on empty returns undefined. Numeric values only.
- RingDeque value: typeof 'number' and not NaN (+/-Infinity accepted).
- UnionFind element: integer in [0, n); fixed n, no growth. Fail closed on a bad
  element (throws [lite-o1]); reset() and forEachRoots() are the O(n) exceptions.
- MonoDeque capacity (power-of-two, rounded up): max simultaneously-live entries;
  push past full throws (fail closed). Value: typeof 'number' and not NaN
  (+/-Infinity accepted). kind frozen at construction. seq ceiling 2^53.
  forEach / [Symbol.iterator] are the O(k) scan exceptions (iterator allocates).

## Scripts

- npm test           -- 119 node:test cases (contract + boundary + differential fuzz).
- npm run test:types -- tsc --noEmit against O1.d.ts.
- npm run torture    -- lite-leak + lite-gc-profiler: 0 B/op, 0 major GC, leak-free.
- npm run witness    -- O(1) throughput-invariance harness + foils + flatness gate.
- npm run test:perf  -- lite-perf-gate hard zero-alloc scavenge-scaling gate.
- npm run verify     -- all five (publish gate).

## Witness gate (locked)

- SparseSet: n-sweep [1e3..1e7] DISPLAYED, batch 1e6, two warm-ups + median of 9.
  The gate is computed over the STEADY window 1e4 <= n <= 1e6: below it (n=1e3) is
  an L1 micro-case that turbo-spikes, above it (n=1e7) is the memory wall where the
  8*n-byte arrays exceed cache and ops/ms measures DRAM, not the algorithm -- both
  are shown but excluded from the gate. SparseSet flatness (opsPerMs last/first over
  the window) >= 0.70; native Set foil flatness <= 0.55 AND SparseSet/Set ops-per-ms
  ratio >= 1.5x at every gated size. (The 0.70 floor is unchanged; only the gate's
  domain is pinned to where ops/ms means O(1).)
- RingDeque: n-sweep [1e3, 1e4, 1e5], FIFO churn vs Array.prototype.shift foil
  (O(n)); ops/ms is a rate, so the ring (batch 5e5) and foil (batch 2e3) use
  different batches yet compare directly. RingDeque flatness >= 0.70; shift foil
  flatness <= 0.55; RingDeque/shift ratio >= 1.5x.
- UnionFind: n-sweep [1e3, 1e4, 1e5], amortized find (coalesced + flattened) vs a
  NAIVE disjoint-set foil (no path compression, no union-by-size -> a degenerate
  chain, O(n) find). ops/ms is a rate (uf batch 5e5, naive batch 2e3). UnionFind
  flatness >= 0.70; naive foil flatness <= 0.55; UnionFind/naive ratio >= 1.5x.
- MonoDeque: W-sweep [1e3, 1e4, 1e5] (W is the sliding-window width), amortized
  push + slide vs a NAIVE window-min that RESCANS the whole window each step
  (O(W)/element). ops/ms is a rate (mono batch 5e5, naive batch 300). MonoDeque
  flatness >= 0.70; naive foil flatness <= 0.55; MonoDeque/naive ratio >= 1.5x.
  The witness also prints the MAX single-op time (an O(W) pop-storm) beside a
  typical O(1) push -- the amortized-honesty bar.

## Not yet shipped

SlotPool and the eight-dimension benchmark suite are on the roadmap, not this
release. A RingLog / overwrite-oldest RingDeque preset is a deferred future
variant. SparseSet holds membership, not payloads (store values in a parallel SoA
column or @zakkster/lite-arena); RingDeque holds numbers only; UnionFind holds
disjoint-set connectivity over [0, n), not payloads; MonoDeque holds numeric
window extremes only (queue integer handles for object payloads).
